newsitem.title: UK: Sinn Fein leader Adams wins British election seat.
newsitem.headline: Sinn Fein leader Adams wins British election seat.

text.p: Gerry Adams, head of the IRA's Sinn Fein political arm, won a Northern Ireland seat in the British parliament on Friday, election officials announced.

Adams was elected for West Belfast, giving Sinn Fein its first parliamentary seat for five years. He beat Joe Hendron of the moderate nationalist Social Democratic and Labour Party who won the seat from Adams in 1992.

Sinn Fein shares the Irish Republican Army's goal of ending Britain's rule over the province. Adams is pledged not to take up his seat in the London legislature because he says that would give recognitions to Britain's right to rule Northern Ireland.

The IRA declared a truce in a 28-year war on British forces in September 1994 but resumed hostilities in February last year accusing Britain of breaking a pledge to bring Sinn Fein into all-party talks.
Britain, supported by the Irish government, says the IRA must abandon violence before it is brought into negotiations.
